title: Agentic Business Process Management: A research manifesto
rationale: Manifesto for governing autonomous agents via explicit process frames with framed autonomy, the central RQ1 construct of binding agents to process models.

title: Multi-Agent Educational System With a Single Large Language Model: an Ablation Study of Memory Configurations and Efficiency
rationale: LLM multi-agent ablation of memory configurations in an educational, non-organizational setting; outcomes are tokens and energy, not policy conformance.

title: A Survey of Large Language Models
rationale: General LLM survey covering pre-training, alignment, and agentic utilization; background only with no process or compliance content.

title: An Interactive Visualization of a Single-LLM Multi-Agent Educational System
rationale: Demo visualization of an educational tutoring multi-agent system; the process is pedagogical rather than organizational and no result is reported.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Automation Patterns for Financial Services using Camunda and Modern Java UIs
rationale: BPMN-orchestrated human-in-the-loop patterns for regulated financial workflows with audit traceability and compliance enforcement, evaluated on workflow metrics.

title: Conversational Enterprise Management Through Agentic AI: A Five-Pillar Framework for LLM-Driven ERP Systems
rationale: LLM multi-agent ERP framework with a security pillar and preliminary validation across finance, HR, and supply-chain scenarios (28/31 criteria).

title: AI Agents and Agentic Systems: A Multi-Expert Analysis
rationale: Multi-expert commentary on agentic systems raising accountability and attribution concerns, but offering no evaluated mechanism or empirical result.

title: Affordance-Compiled Intelligence: Observable-Only Cognitive Impedance Matching for No-Meta LLM-Integrated Systems
rationale: Theory of world-side constraints (validators, authority scopes, conformance envelopes, rollback, audit receipts) for constraining fixed LLM policies; no empirical test.

title: COLA: Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework with Dynamic Task Scheduling for GUI Automation
rationale: Multi-agent GUI automation with dynamic scheduling and an interactive backtracking repair mechanism, benchmarked on GAIA and WindowsAgentArena for task completion.

title: Formal verification of time-bounded BPMN model with message broker using timed automata
rationale: Pre-LLM formal verification of time-bounded BPMN via timed automata and UPPAAL; anchors the deterministic process-model baseline without agent content.

title: Context is key for cybersecurity: leveraging external knowledge for process model explanation via LLMs
rationale: Combines BPMN process models with ISO 27001/IEC 62443 via modular prompting for LLM compliance checking, evaluated on two IIoT cases with a compliance error typology.

title: From chat to process: A conversational agent framework for social business process management
rationale: Conversational multi-agent framework covering the BPM lifecycle with intent detection and process memory, illustrated on a call-for-tenders use case.

title: Generative AI–Enhanced Business Process Modeling in Governmental Organizations: Opportunities and Challenges
rationale: Conceptual analysis of GenAI in public-sector BPM naming governance controls, HITL oversight, and explainability as risk responses without evaluating any of them.

title: Theorizing the Evolution of RPA-ERP Integration: A Three-Dimensional Model
rationale: Conceptual three-dimensional model of RPA-ERP evolution from rule-based bots to cognitive agents; background on the deterministic automation baseline.

title: Agentic Hyperautomation: A Distributed Architecture for Scalable AI-Driven Workflows
rationale: LLM orchestrator dynamically planning and delegating to specialized tool-using agents, explicitly replacing pre-defined workflows, shown via a document-management case study.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Agents for Computer Use: Foundations, Challenges, and Future Directions
rationale: Survey of 87 computer-use agent papers and 33 datasets identifying non-standardized evaluation and low benchmark task complexity as field-wide limitations.

title: A Multi-Criteria Decision Framework for Enterprise LLM Routing
rationale: Enterprise LLM router with confidence margin and risk veto evaluated on 500 business prompts against seven baselines, trading cost against response sufficiency.

title: A Systematic Review of Generative AI Applications in Process Mining: Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions
rationale: PRISMA review of 24 GenAI process-mining studies reporting fragmented evidence, limited standardized benchmarking, and trust concerns.

title: Analyzing structural and semantic similarities between formal business process models using ChatGPT-5.1: a test report
rationale: Tests whether an LLM detects seeded structural and semantic deviations in BPMN models, showing accuracy depends on standardized representation and prompting.

title: Advanced Multilingual Natural Language Processing in Industrial Digitalization: A Case Study of Autonomous Document Classification and ERP Integration in Manufacturing
rationale: Deployed LLM document-classification system integrated with ERP, reporting a measured manual baseline error rate, per-decision rationales, and data-sanitization controls.

title: Human-artificial interaction in the age of agentic AI: a system-theoretical approach
rationale: System-theoretic framework for human-agent coordination using Petri nets and communication spaces; formal background with no compliance evaluation.

title: ProAgent: From Robotic Process Automation to Agentic Process Automation
rationale: Foundational agentic process automation paper where LLM agents construct and execute workflows in place of rigid RPA, with experiments on construction and execution.

title: AI Agents Under Threat: A Survey of Key Security Challenges and Future Pathways
rationale: Survey of AI agent security threats naming unpredictable multi-step inputs and untrusted external entities as failure sources relevant to agent control design.

title: On the potential of large language models to solve semantics-aware process mining tasks
rationale: Benchmarks LLMs on five semantics-aware process-mining tasks, showing out-of-the-box and in-context use fails where fine-tuning succeeds.

title: ФУНКЦИОНАЛЬНАЯ АРХИТЕКТУРА БИЗНЕС-СИСТЕМЫ КАК ОСНОВА МОДЕЛИРОВАНИЯ И РАЗВИТИЯ ОРГАНИЗАЦИИ
rationale: Russian-language article on functional architecture of business systems with no LLM, agent, or compliance-control content.

title: PPIPilot: Automating the suggestion and computation of Process Performance Indicators from event logs
rationale: LLM pipeline suggesting and computing process performance indicators from event logs, with a fallback mechanism empirically shown to reduce computation failures.

title: Business Process Reengineering in the Age of Generative and Agentic AI: Translation, Persistence, and Renewed Relevance
rationale: Management-fashion perspective on BPR resurfacing under agentic AI; conceptual framing of process redesign with no mechanism or evaluation.

title: Integrating LLM in Business Process Management: A Conceptual Framework for Augmenting the Process Lifecycle
rationale: Lifecycle governance framework allocating LLM use by risk with NIST/EU AI Act controls, plus a BPI-2017 stress test exposing control-flow mismatch against an event-log referent.

title: A Review on Edge Large Language Models: Design, Execution, and Applications
rationale: Survey of edge deployment and inference optimization for LLMs; wrong field with no process, agent, or compliance dimension.

title: Design principles for process improvement and innovation systems
rationale: Design-science principles for human-facing process improvement and innovation systems; BPM background predating the agentic control question.

title: Providing Domain Knowledge for Process Mining with ReWOO-Based Agents
rationale: Proof-of-concept ReWOO agent injecting domain knowledge into process mining tool interactions across several business processes.

title: Encouraging Divergent Thinking in Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Debate
rationale: Multi-agent debate with a judge as a generic reliability control for LLM reasoning, evaluated against self-reflection baselines on two datasets.

title: Process model forecasting and change exploration using time series analysis of event sequence data
rationale: Time-series forecasting of whole process models from event logs; pre-LLM process analytics background with no agent or policy element.

title: MCIP: Protecting MCP Safety via Model Contextual Integrity Protocol
rationale: Protocol-level integrity control for tool-using LLM agents, with an unsafe-behavior taxonomy plus benchmark and training data showing measurable safety gains.

title: KI-basierte Prozessanalyse
rationale: German-language short paper on an LLM/RAG chatbot generating BPMN diagrams from interviews; excluded as non-English per protocol.
